oliver: quick question — noticed a discrepancy between Python SDK and the REST API for the /v1/generate endpoint. Python SDK sends `temperature` by default but the TS SDK serializes as `temp`. Which is our canonical param?

devon: hmm we standardized on `temperature` in the API spec last year, but I remember a legacy `temp` alias for some older clients. where did you see `temp` coming from?

oliver: found it in the TS SDK serialization code. example: `client.generate({ prompt, temp: 0.7 })` ends up as `{ temp: 0.7 }` in the JSON body. curl example from REST docs uses `{"temperature":0.7}`.

lina: can you paste the snippets?

oliver: sure — Python usage:```
# python
client.generate(prompt="hi") # uses default temperature=0.9 in SDK config
# actual payload -> {"temperature":0.9}
```
TS usage:```
// typescript
client.generate({ prompt: 'hi' }) // default temp = 0.9 in SDK config
// actual payload -> { temp: 0.9 }
```

sam: oh yikes. that explains a few QA failures where evals saw slightly different outputs between SDKs. said differently: same numerical value but different key name could be accepted by the runtime (we currently accept both) — but some middleware (rate limiting/proxy) normalizes bodies and expects `temperature`.

maria: runtime currently accepts both `temp` and `temperature` for backwards compat, but our telemetry and request hashing use the canonical `temperature` key which means `temp` clients bypass some caching logic. that affects perf and cost numbers.

oliver: exactly. impact: 1) customers using TS SDK might miss caching benefits 2) tests that assert request body keys fail 3) confusion on defaults.

devon: proposal: make `temperature` canonical in the API and SDKs; accept `temp` for 2 release cycles with a deprecation warning header `X-Deprecated-Param: temp`. update API spec and add a migration note.

lina: +1. also we should add serialization tests in the SDK repo matrix (python/ts) to assert canonical key in outgoing JSON. I can add a test case. @sam can you update the TS serializer to prefer `temperature` when both exist?

sam: yep. plan: change the TS SDK to serialize `temperature` in the body. keep `temp` as alias in the parsing layer for incoming calls. add changelog entry and a short migration snippet. target patch release for SDKs next week.

maria: I'll add server-side deprecation header and log telemetry for `temp` usage. after 2 releases we can remove parsing alias. also recommend a feature-flagged rollout for switching cache keys so we can measure impact.

api-bot: deploy-checklist created: https://infra.redwood/internal/tasks/INFR-8213 (tests: sdk-serialization, deprecation-header, caching-metrics)

devon: sounds good. owners: @sam (ts sdk), @oliver (python sdk verification), @lina (sdk tests), @maria (runtime deprecation + cache rollout). ETA: TS SDK patch by Tue, Python verification same week, server header + telemetry by Fri.

oliver: I'll run a quick compatibility script against our private staging to count how many `temp` users remain. will post results here. :thumbsup:

lina: thanks — if anyone has examples of other param mismatches (e.g., `max_tokens` vs `maxTokens`) ping here and we'll batch changes.

sam: one small note — there are also enum serializations differences for `format` (string vs nested object). I'll open a follow-up thread for that.

oliver: perfect. thanks everyone.
